title: RN start of care, cooperative patient with spouse

turns.text: Good morning, Mr. Briggs. I'm Maya, the nurse from the home health agency. Is it okay if we go through some questions for your start of care today?
Sure, sure. Call me Walt. June made coffee if you want some.
That's kind, thank you. Let's start simple. Can you tell me your date of birth?
February ninth, nineteen forty-four. No, wait. Forty-five. February ninth, nineteen forty-five. I always do that.
It's forty-five, honey. He's eighty-one.
Got it. And what language do you prefer to speak with your doctors?
English. Just English.
Would you ever want an interpreter for your appointments?
No, no need.
Are you of Hispanic, Latino, or Spanish origin?
No, ma'am.
And how would you describe your race?
White.
What insurance is covering the home care? Is it regular Medicare, or one of the Advantage plans?
Regular Medicare, the original kind. We don't have one of those Advantage plans.
Who lives here with you, Walt?
Just me and June. Fifty-six years.
And is June around most of the time, day and night?
I'm here all the time. I don't drive anymore, so I'm always home.
Before this hospital stay, how were you doing with bathing, dressing, getting to the toilet, and eating? Did you need any help?
No, I did all that myself. June just made sure I ate my vegetables.
What about walking from room to room before you got sick?
Fine. I used a cane outside sometimes, but in the house I walked on my own.
And stairs? You've got that staircase up to the bedroom.
I needed June's hand on the stairs since last winter. She'd walk behind me.
Did you use a walker or a wheelchair before all this?
No walker, no wheelchair. Just the cane I mentioned.
Who handled things like planning your shopping or keeping track of your pills?
I did my own pills. June writes the shopping lists, but I could do it.

Okay. Now I'm going to check your memory a little. I am going to say three words for you to remember. Please repeat the words after I have said all three. The words are sock, blue, and bed. Now tell me the three words.
Sock, blue... bed.
Perfect. Please tell me what year it is right now.
Twenty twenty-six.
What month are we in right now?
End of September. The leaves are turning.
And what day of the week is today?
Tuesday? No... Monday. It's Monday, right June?
Don't look at me, you're the one being tested.
Monday. Final answer.
Over the past 5 days, how much of the time has pain made it hard for you to sleep at night?
The knee keeps me up a few nights. Not every night. I'd say now and then.
And over those 5 days, how often have you cut back on your day-to-day activities because of the pain?
Pretty often, honestly. I skipped my walk to the mailbox most days.
Do you get short of breath? When does it happen?
Only on the stairs, or if I walk to the end of the driveway. Sitting here, I'm fine.
How often do you feel lonely or isolated from those around you?
Lonely? With June here? Never. Our grandson calls every Sunday.
Have you had any falls in the past year?
One. I slipped in the garage in March and broke my wrist.
How many times have you been in the hospital in the last six months?
Just this once, for the knee replacement.
Let's go through your medications. What are you taking right now?
I have the list. Metoprolol, lisinopril, the atorvastatin, aspirin, the Eliquis since the surgery, and oxycodone for the knee, only at night.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual, like exhausted?
Tired after the surgery, sure, but not exhausted. I'm getting my energy back.
Last thing, let's get your height and weight. Can you step on the scale for me?
Here goes nothing.
One eighty-seven point four. And you're five eleven, right?
Five eleven. Used to be six foot.
Great. That's everything for today's assessment. I'll see you Thursday.

notes: Traps: birth-year self-correction; cane is not a GG0110 device (so Z); final weekday answer Monday is wrong (visit is Tuesday); 6 medications triggers M1033 code 7; 187.4 rounds down.
